chunks: Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:

You may give the adhan while not being in a state of wudu (ablution), in a single garment, standing or sitting, and whichever direction you face. But when you perform the iqamah, then do so in a state of wudu, prepared for the salat (prayer).

key_terms.أَقَمْتَ: you perform the iqamah, the second call immediately preceding prayer
key_terms.تُؤَذِّنُ: you give the adhan, the call announcing the time of prayer
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ: a single garment, indicating minimal clothing suffices here
key_terms.قَائِمًا: standing, one permitted posture for giving the adhan
key_terms.قَاعِدًا: sitting, also permitted for giving the adhan
key_terms.لِلصَّلَاةِ: for the salat (prayer), indicating immediate preparation for worship
key_terms.مُتَهَيِّئًا: prepared and ready, meaning in a state of readiness for the prayer
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), ritual purification before prayer-related acts

ai.seo_question: Is wudu required for adhan and iqamah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal distinction between the adhan and the iqamah. It permits the adhan without wudu (ablution), in a single garment, whether standing or sitting, and facing any direction, while requiring that the iqamah be performed in a state of wudu and readiness for salat (prayer).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.866 - Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said:

"You may give the adhan (call to prayer) without being in a state of wudu (ritual purity), wearing a single garment, whether standing or sitting, and in any direction you face.
However, when you perform the iqamah (second call to prayer), you must be in a state of wudu, prepared for the prayer."
